newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Energy to acquire American Enviro.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Energy to acquire American Enviro.

text.p: U.S. Energy Systems Inc on Monday said it would acquire American Enviro-Services Inc, an environmental services company in Newburgh, Indiana, in a deal valued at about $3.3 million.
American Enviro-Services will operate as a subsidiary of U.S. Energy, forming the nucleus of a new division called USE-Environmental.
U.S. Energy said it expected the new division "to contribute significantly to revenues" and enhance its independent power and cogeneration business.

U.S. Energy develops, owns and operates cogeneration and independent power projects. American Enviro-Services collects and recycles used motor and industrial oils, and produces fuel used in industrial furnaces, boilers, and electric cogeneration systems.
"It adds an important dimension to our company, and we add an important dimension to theirs and allow them to expand at much faster rate," U.S. Energy President Richard Nelson said.
Nelson said his company would take a goodwill charge annually for the acquisition and that the deal should help earnings.
"I see it adding to earnings...it will be positive and substantial," Nelson said, though he declined to give specific estimates.
Howard Nevins will continue as president and chief executive of American Enviro-Services and also become executive vice president of U.S. Energy Systems in charge of the new environmental division.

"Joining the U.S. Energy Systems team will allow operations to expand faster over a larger geographic area through internal growth and acquisitions," Nevins said in a company statement. "We intend to be a major player nationwide in all segments of our industry, and especially in the recycled oil industry."
Trading in U.S. Energy shares were halted Monday morning at 3-3/4.
